units: $ million, accrual (GFS) expenses, Australian Government general government sector, actual outcomes
notes: Values are $ million, nominal, accrual GFS expenses of the Australian Government general government sector. Method: for each year Y the actual is taken from the 'Expenses by function and sub-function' appendix of the Budget Paper No. 1 published two budgets later (Y+2), which is the latest place each year's actual appears in a BP1; spot checks show identical figures to the later Final Budget Outcome comparatives where those exist (e.g. 2023-24 in FBO 2024-25, 2024-25 in FBO 2025-26). Exceptions: 1999-00 comes from the 1999-2000 Final Budget Outcome (Table 2, GFS basis) because no later BP1 reports a 1999-00 actual by function; 2018-19 comes from the 2019-20 FBO because the 2020-21 Budget was delayed to October 2020 and reported 2019-20 rather than 2018-19 as its actual year; 2025-26 (beyond the requested range) comes from the 2025-26 Final Budget Outcome (published September 2026). CLASSIFICATION BREAKS: (1) 1999-00 is not fully comparable with later years: it was the first year published on a GFS basis, nominal superannuation interest was not split out of General public services (Government superannuation benefits), Other purposes includes the pre-GST Financial Assistance Grants to the states and an 'Asset sales' sub-function, Fuel and energy is tiny (fuel subsidies such as the diesel fuel rebate/fuel credits appear as expenses only from 2000-01), and aged care sits on an earlier Health/Social security split. (2) GST payments to the states are EXCLUDED from expenses for 1999-00 to 2005-06 (GST was then treated as a state tax) and INCLUDED in Other purposes (General purpose inter-government transactions) from 2006-07 onward; this is why Other purposes jumps from about $13bn (2005-06) to about $52bn (2006-07) and total expenses jumps by about $40bn. (3) From 2000-01 assistance to the aged was reclassified from Health to Social security and welfare. (4) Each year carries the classification used in the budget that published it, so smaller sub-function reclassifications appear as level shifts (e.g. Australian Health Care Agreements -> National Healthcare SPP (2009-10) -> National Health Reform payments (2010-11 onward), harmonised here as 'Assistance to the states for public hospitals'; 'Pharmaceutical services and benefits' renamed; old 'Other health services' aggregate mapped to 'Health services'; 'Aboriginal advancement nec' mapped to 'Assistance for Indigenous Australians nec'; 'Common youth allowance' and 'Health assistance to the aged' were discontinued after 2008-09 and their expenses folded into other sub-functions). (5) The 2008-09 BP1 reported 2006-07 'Hospital services' combined with health care agreements; the split for 2006-07 (1,549 hospital services / 8,867 health care agreements) is taken from the 2006-07 FBO (same Health total 39,948). Large one-off movements are genuine outcomes, not parsing errors: 2008-09 and 2009-10 stimulus (Social security, Education BER), 2019-20 to 2020-21 JobKeeper (Other economic affairs), 2024-25 one-offs in Health services and Assistance to veterans, 2025-26 jump in Education (Student assistance). Subfunctions: Education 'Schools' already includes its Government/Non-government schools components (not listed separately to avoid double counting). Subfunction series are null where a sub-function did not exist in that year's classification; for 1999-00 only Other purposes sub-functions are available. Rounding: the 14 functions sum to Total expenses within +/-3 in every year (see sum_checks).
